subject: CALL statement
notes: CLOSED 2026-10-16 (kb/Work PB258, wave 1102 E). cite.py --check 14.9.4.3 'If the BY REFERENCE phrase is specified or implied for an identifier-2 and identifier-2 is not an address-identifier, it is a receiving operand.' -> OK, Syntax rules 5. || BOTH ARMS OF THE CONDITION ARE NOW WITNESSED. The plain arm (identifier-2 BY REFERENCE, specified or implied, is RECEIVING): conformance:cases/14.9.4-CALL/l1_call_by_reference_receiving_operand (REF=0015 / BARE=0025 / CON=0030, the BY CONTENT contrast of SR4) and the receiving-screen side conformance:cases/14.9.4-CALL/pb128-call-constant-by-reference (13.18.15.3 SR2 through ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving). The EXCEPTION arm ('and identifier-2 is not an address-identifier'), which this row held PARTIAL because no address-identifier could be WRITTEN as a CALL argument, became writable when kb/Work PB239 landed the addressIdentifier operand (rows SR-14.9.4.3-3/-4); CallBinder.BindCall's BY REFERENCE arm takes AddressArg before the receiving chokepoint, so an address-identifier never meets ResolveReceiving (8.4.3.11.3 SR5 / 8.4.3.13.3 SR4: 'This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand'). || THE DISCRIMINATING GOLDEN this row named as its closing condition: conformance:cases/14.9.4-CALL/pb258_call_address_identifier_sending puts an address-identifier and an ordinary identifier-2 BY REFERENCE in ONE statement, specified and then implied (14.9.4.4 GR5 in Format 1; GR9 a)1 in Format 2), and the callee stores into both formals. Format 1 (ADDRESS OF R with N PIC 9(4)): N=0015 then N=0020 while the address formal's SET TO NULL reaches nothing (the second call reads LR=XYZ). Format 2, where SR10's class-pointer ban does not apply, so both arguments are of class pointer and differ ONLY in being an address-identifier: data arm PA>XYZLO / PP=NULL after P received the first call's store (P=NULL); program arm TARGET CALLED / QP=NULL after Q received it (Q=NULL). Measured identical at --std 2002, 2014 and 2023 on the worktree's built compiler; below 2002 an address-identifier operand is the edition gate's (conformance:cases/14.9.4-CALL/pb239-call-address-identifier-at-85). Editions: the plain arm holds at all four; the exception arm exists from 2002.
